Japanese_defense.other_labor_aviation_support: roughly 450-520 persons, many armed late or used in support
Japanese_defense.weapons: historical count family retained: 120mm coastal guns, 75mm mountain guns, 81mm mortars, 37mm AT, MG/grenade dischargers
branch_change: 3-4 extra preparation days after historical clock plus mature Branch fortification/QC practice
better alternate positions, ammo dispersion, wire/radio redundancy and registered mortar lanes
two Type95 centered mobile/revetment-capable rather than all treated as static pillboxes

US_bombardment.effect: heavy and tactically decisive; coastal guns largely suppressed before landing
US_bombardment.one_120mm_survival: one gun/position may fire 3-6 effective rounds before suppression; no US combatant hit centered
US_bombardment.air_support: 2 CVL + 3 CVE strike/CAP cycles; lower high-end fast-carrier mass than historical Saratoga+2CVL but adequate against a fighterless island

night_gate.result: no second organized battalion-scale attack; 20-50-man pockets/infiltrators, ammo movement and wounded recovery continue until dawn

armor_exchange.mechanism: Type95 37mm and mines are dangerous to amphibian vehicles/flanks but lose rapidly to M4/75mm, naval fire and infantry-engineer reduction.

casualties_working.source_guard: Historical published Engebi casualty series conflict materially (notably wounded totals). Branch uses a wide event band rather than pretending one series is exact.

systemic_effect.Branch_tank_days: increase enemy casualties and LVT disruption but final Japanese tank residual remains zero because the island is lost
systemic_effect.US_cost: extra hours consume naval shells, carrier sorties, tank ammunition and infantry fatigue
systemic_effect.schedule: does not delay the Eniwetok Island assault beyond 22 Feb because the 22d Marines can reorganize/reembark while mop-up continues
